first.label: failure_to_yield
first.where: cw2, the zebra across the outbound carriageway from the median tip / island_round to the right kerb (x~1195-1850, y~470-545)
first.description: The main road was red, so the cross street had its phase. Vehicles from the right queued below cw2 while pedestrians crossed. From 12.5 s they drove up-left through cw2 one after another, with no gap, while late pedestrians were still on the zebra: three white Chevrolet Cobalt/Lacetti sedans, a grey Malibu and a white Damas van, then a black Lacetti, a black SUV and a turquoise delivery scooter (purple jacket). The first Cobalt entered at 12.5 s and cut about 1 m in front of a woman in white who was walking toward it (12.75-13.25 s). The second Cobalt and a Lacetti passed right beside two girls in black and a blonde woman on the zebra (13.75-16.0 s). At 18.25-19.25 s the black Lacetti and the black SUV passed right in front of the two girls at the kerb end of the zebra, and the scooter rode off the kerb beside them. The segment ends when the SUV and the scooter leave the zebra (~19.9-20.0 s), as the girls step onto the kerb.

verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:
The event is real and failure_to_yield is the right label. I checked the zebra's position on an empty frame at 22.0 s: cw2 runs from the island_round at about (1200-1310, 505-540) to the right kerb at about (1830, 474-500). The main-road signal inset shows red for the whole 0-21.5 s window, which is the cross-street and cw1/cw2 pedestrian phase.

Context: pedestrians were already crossing cw2 at 0 s. From 5.5 to 8.5 s, white Cobalts and Lacettis coming from the right queued below cw2. The lead Cobalt stopped with its bumper about 20 px short of the zebra's lower edge, so the queue yielded at first and nothing is a violation before 12 s.

Start: the lead Cobalt did not move from 10.5 to 12.0 s. It began creeping at about 12.2 s. At that moment a woman in a white top and black trousers was about 80 px up-left of its bumper, directly in its path, walking right toward the kerb. Two girls (black and burgundy clothes), a blonde woman and a pair near the island were also on the zebra. In the 6.7x zoom:
- 12.6 s: the hood overlaps the first stripes on screen.
- 12.8 s: the bottom of the front bumper reaches the zebra's lower edge.
- ~13.2 s: the car's front ground point is inside the zebra (estimated from the front-wheel contact at 1374,563 at 13.0 s and 1309,539 at 13.6 s).
- 13.2 s: the Cobalt passes about 35-40 px (roughly 1-1.5 m) behind the woman in white, who had just crossed its path.
I put the start at 12.8 s, when the bumper visibly enters the crossing. The first-pass 12.5 s marks when the car's image first overlaps the stripes; the ground-contact entry is about 13.1-13.2 s.

Middle: vehicles kept crossing cw2 from right to up-left with no gap while the two girls walked slowly along it, from x≈1450 at 13 s to ≈1580 at 15 s, ≈1705 at 17.25 s and ≈1830 at 19.6 s, feet staying inside the zebra band. In order: the second Cobalt (13.5-14.5 s), a Lacetti whose front passed about 25 px below and behind the girls (15.0-15.5 s), a grey Malibu (15.5-16.75 s), a white Damas (16.25-17.75 s), a white modern sedan (17.25-18.6 s), then a black Lacetti and a black SUV (from about 18.2 s). The blonde woman reached the right end at about 15.5 s.

End: at 18.8-19.2 s the black Lacetti's rear (x≈1795) passed less than 1 m from the girls (x≈1800-1825, feet y≈490, on the zebra near the kerb end). A delivery scooter (purple jacket, teal box) came off the kerb or parking pocket by the parked white Cobalt and rode along the zebra's upper part right beside them. The Lacetti's rear cleared the upper edge at about 19.3-19.4 s and the scooter at about 19.7-19.8 s. The black SUV's rear wheel was on the upper edge at 19.8 s and its rear bumper had cleared by about 20.0 s. The girls reached the kerb at about 19.9-20.2 s. End = 20.0 s, give or take 0.2 s.

Rejected / doubtful:
- The white Cobalt that crossed cw2 at 20.3-21.3 s had no pedestrian on the zebra (the girls were on the pavement), so it is excluded.
- The woman in white left the zebra's upper edge at about 15 s and walked up-right on the carriageway or its edge next to the parked Cobalt (x≈1480-1730, y≈440-480, 15-22 s). This could be jaywalking, but I did not verify it and the kerb line there is unclear (low confidence).
- The pair walking left to the island at 12-13.5 s were not near any vehicle.

On the class itself: this is a stream of cross-street vehicles turning through a crossing that pedestrians use during the same signal phase. It meets the brief's literal definition ("drives through a crossing while a pedestrian is on it"), with two clear close passes: about 13.2 s and 18.8-19.4 s.

first.label: failure_to_yield
first.where: cw3, the zebra across the lower-left side street, ridden from the top-left kerb (x~150, y~760) down to the bottom edge of the frame (x~700-800, y~1080)
first.description: An orange delivery scooter (purple jacket, red helmet) came off the left kerb onto the zebra at 44.75 s and rode down its length while two men (navy and brown shirts) were walking up it the other way. It passed within about 0.5 m of them at 46.5-47.5 s and left the zebra at the bottom frame edge at ~50.5 s. A man with a backpack was also stepping onto the zebra at the end. Low confidence only because the scooter rode ALONG the crossing like a pedestrian rather than across it; the facts themselves are clear.

verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:
I checked this myself with a 0.5 s sheet over 40.8-54.5, 0.2 s crops at the top-left kerb end of cw3 (44.0-45.8), at the pass (45.8-47.6) and at the bottom edge (49.6-51.2), a 0.1 s crop at 50.3-50.8, and full-resolution crops at 44.6, 44.8 and 45.2.

Signal: the bottom (green) lamp of the main-road head is lit through the whole window. That is the cw3 pedestrian phase, so the pedestrians had right of way.

Pedestrians: from 40.8 s two men (navy shirt, brown shirt) walk up cw3 on the stripes, from the bottom toward the top-left kerb. At 45-46 s they are at about frame (490-520, 770-840), in the middle of the zebra.

Scooter: an orange delivery scooter (purple jacket, red helmet, orange top box) waits on the sidewalk by the bins at 44.0 s (front wheel about x140, y775). At 44.6 s it is off the kerb on the asphalt, just left of the stripe ends. At 44.8 s its front wheel reaches the lower-left edge of the zebra stripes. That is my start, which matches the first pass's 44.75. From 45.2 s it is on the stripes and rides down the length of the crossing, straight toward the two men. It does not stop or visibly slow, and the men keep walking. At 46.6-47.2 s it passes right beside the navy-shirt man, roughly 0.5-1 m away (my estimate for the gap is a bit wider than the first pass's 0.5 m). It is between/next to both men at 46.8-47.0. It then carries on down the stripes (48-50 s, about x 650-800, y 950-1050), still inside cw3. The wheels go off the bottom frame edge at about 50.2-50.4. The rider's helmet is last seen at 50.6-50.7 and is gone at 50.8. So the scooter leaves the crossing at the frame edge, and I set the end at 50.6. A man with a backpack (white shirt) is at the bottom-right edge of cw3 at 50.0-51.2, standing just beside the zebra's right edge and about to step onto it.

Class decision: the brief says scooter riders are vehicles. This one drove through a crossing (it entered one end and left at the other) while pedestrians were on it, and passed within arm's length without yielding. That fits the literal failure_to_yield definition. No other class fits: jaywalking is excluded because the rider counts as a vehicle, near_miss needs braking or a swerve (there was none), and wrong_way does not apply.

Why medium and not high: the scooter rode ALONG the zebra, in the pedestrians' own direction of travel, instead of crossing it the way a car does. Its path ran next to the men rather than cutting across it. The organizers' ground truth may not count this pattern. The facts themselves are unambiguous.

first.label: failure_to_yield
first.where: cw3, the lower half (the side-street entry just left of island_3, x~530-850, y~900-1080)
first.description: A black Chevrolet Trailblazer SUV had crawled through the congested junction from the approach. It turned right and west into the lower-left side street, entered cw3 at ~53.5 s and accelerated across it without braking. A pedestrian with a backpack (white shirt) was mid-zebra walking up-left, and the SUV passed about 1-2 m from him (54.25-55.0 s). The SUV's rear cleared the zebra at ~55.3 s. The pedestrian took no evasive action (not a near miss).

verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:
I checked this myself with an overview sheet from 49.5 to 58.0 s at 0.5 s steps. I then zoomed in on cw3 at 0.25 s steps (52.0-56.25 s) and at 0.1 s steps around the entry (53.0-53.8 s, plus a tight crop on the bumper at 53.3-53.7 s) and the exit (55.0-55.8 s).

Signal: the vehicle inset shows the bottom (green) lamp lit through the whole window. The main road is green, which is the normal walking phase for cw3, so the pedestrian had right of way against right-turners.

Pedestrian: a young man in a white shirt with a dark backpack, carrying a navy bag. He is on the cw3 zebra the whole time, walking from bottom-right to top-left. At ~51-52 s he is at the lower end (about x 790-870, y 1020-1066). At 53.5 s he is at about (705, 930), at 54.25 s about (660, 880), and at 57+ s he is still on the zebra.

Vehicle: a black Chevrolet Trailblazer SUV turning right out of the congested junction. From 52.0 to 53.0 s it creeps forward, then from about 53.3 s it speeds up leftward along the bottom of the frame (about y 900-1080). It crosses the lower part of cw3 without stopping. At 53.7-53.8 s its front bumper is roughly 80 image px (about 1-1.5 m) to the right of the pedestrian's feet. At 54.25-55.0 s it passes right beside him: his feet are just on the far side of the SUV body.

This fits failure_to_yield as the brief defines it: a vehicle drives through a crossing while a pedestrian is on it. One caveat: the SUV passed through the part of the zebra he had left about 1.5 s earlier, so it went behind him rather than into his path. The brief's definition does not require the pedestrian to be in the vehicle's path, so this still counts. It is not a near_miss. The pedestrian did not dodge and kept his pace, and the SUV did not brake or swerve sharply.

Timing:
- Start (front of the SUV reaches the painted stripes): in the bumper zoom, at 53.3 s the bumper is just short of where the stripes end. At 53.4 s the front bumper, at about full-frame (850, 1020), is at the stripe edge, and by 53.5-53.6 s it overlaps the stripes. Start = 53.4 s, within about 0.1 s.
- End (rear of the SUV clears the stripes): at 55.2 s the rear bumper and tail light are exactly at the left edge of the stripes. At 55.3 s the rear is clearly past them. End = 55.25 s.

The first-pass times (53.5 and 55.3 s) agree with mine to within about 0.1 s.

first.label: illegal_u_turn
first.where: junction east of the median tip (x~1550-1760, y~560-630), then up through cw2 into the outbound carriageway
first.description: A white Lacetti/Gentra taxi with yellow Yandex livery, from the approach (crossed the stop line on green ~42 s). It drifted left into the junction heading east (43.5-46 s) and waited there for the oncoming flow from the right (46-57 s). It then swung round at 57.0 s (heading north at 58.0 s) and was settled up-left in the outbound at ~59.25 s, passing cw2 with no pedestrians on it. Low confidence: no sign or marking prohibiting the U-turn can be seen (the signs face away from the camera), and the manoeuvre looked like an ordinary yielding U-turn. If the pre-positioning counts, the start could be taken as ~43.5 s.

verdict.label: illegal_u_turn
verdict.reasoning:
The manoeuvre is real, but nothing shows it is prohibited, so it does not meet the illegal_u_turn definition ("U-turn where markings/signs prohibit it").

What I saw:
- 53-57 s (full sheet, then crop 1100-380-1920-780 at 0.25 s steps): the white Lacetti/Gentra Yandex taxi stands in the junction east of the median tip, pointing right (east), next to a white Matiz. Other vehicles from the approach are lined up the same way. The signal inset is green the whole time.
- 57.0-57.25 s: the taxi starts to swing.
- 57.5 s: rear toward the camera, heading up-right. 58.0-58.25 s: heading straight up (north), east of the round island.
- 58.5-59.4 s: heading up-left through cw2 into the outbound.
- ~59.6-60.0 s: aligned with the outbound lanes and moving away.
- If it had counted, the turn would be ~57.0 to ~59.6 s.

Why it is not illegal:
1. No prohibiting sign or marking is visible. The zoom of the approach lanes (work/eda/zoom_approach_lanes.jpg) shows no lane-direction arrows at the stop line. The gantry carries only a priority-road diamond, seen from behind. I cannot see any no-U-turn sign.
2. The only sign facing U-turners is the blue "keep right" sign on the round island at (1280,515). It faces north-bound traffic, which here means the U-turners. They pass it on the right, as this taxi did. That points to a channelised, allowed movement, not a banned one.
3. work/eda/uturn_od.jpg shows about 10 tracks doing exactly this U-turn along the same loop around the island (x~1500-1830). It is a routine movement at this junction, and the flow field shows it as a regular pattern too. Another yellow taxi at 41-48 s used the same left/U-turn pocket.
4. It was done on green from the left side of the approach, and the taxi waited for the oncoming flow from the right (46-57 s). Under Uzbek rules, as under the Russian ones, that is an ordinary permitted U-turn at a junction unless a sign forbids it.

Other classes I checked and rejected:
- failure_to_yield: cw2 was checked at 0.2 s steps from 58.4 to 60.0 s (crop 1150-400-1920-640). No pedestrian is on the crossing; the only people are on the far sidewalk.
- illegal_turn: no evidence of a wrong lane or banned direction.
- wrong_way: it entered the outbound in the correct direction.
- red_light: it crossed the stop line on green.
- The ~43.5 s pre-positioning is only lawful waiting inside the junction.

first.label: stop_line
first.where: approach stop zone and cw1, centre lanes (x~690-975, y~460-630)
first.description: The main-road signal turned red at 66.07 s. At that moment two cars were standing past the approach stop line without having entered the junction, because the gridlocked junction blocked them. A white sedan (stopped since ~59-60 s) filled the stop zone with its nose ~18 px onto cw1. A black sedan (stopped ~65.0 s during yellow) stood on cw1. The white sedan pulled on into the junction at ~71.5-72 s, still on red; it had crossed the line on green, so this is not red_light. The black sedan moved forward at ~76-78 s but stayed straddling cw1 (front just into the junction) through the rest of the red; pedestrians walked around it. The segment ends when the signal turns green at 102.1 s. If 'vehicle stops' is read literally, the start could be 65.0 s. Two other cars overhang the line by only ~0.3-0.5 m and were not counted on their own: a white Lacetti (stopped ~64.5 s until after 102 s) and a white sedan (until ~72.5 s).

verdict.label: stop_line
verdict.reasoning:
Signal (checked at 0.1 s on the median head crop 1120-355-1200-425): yellow is lit up to 66.0 s and red is first clearly lit at 66.1 s. Red+yellow shows at 100.1-102.0 s and green first appears at 102.1 s. So red runs from about 66.05 to 102.05 s.

Main vehicle, a black Mitsubishi sedan in the centre lane (frame x~700-900, y~470-600):
- 56 s and 60 s, green: its front is already past the white stop line (stop line at crop y~200 vs its front at ~290 in the 280-360-1240-720 zoom). It is creeping in a gridlocked queue behind a black BYD that is stuck in the junction.
- 64.4-65.15 s (0.25 s crop): it stops at about 64.6-65.0 s, during yellow. The whole body is between the stop line and cw1, with the front at cw1's upper edge.
- 66.1-76.6 s: it stays stationary there.
- 76.6-78.1 s: it creeps about 45 px forward.
- 78-104 s: it straddles cw1, with the rear in the stop zone and the front bumper at or just past cw1's lower edge, almost touching the BYD. It is never fully in the junction. A 90.0 s full-res crop confirms this.
- 82-100 s: pedestrians crossing on red walk around it on cw1 and the stop zone.
- It is still there at 104 s, after green.

It crossed the line on green, so this is not red_light. It is stationary past the stop line through the whole red without entering the intersection, which fits stop_line. It also fits better than congestion or stopped_vehicle.

A second car, the white Lacetti in the right-centre lane, is also stopped past the line with its nose about 10 px onto cw1 at red onset (stopped since about 60 s). It pulls into the junction at 71.6-72.1 s. Being the same class at the same time, it belongs in the same segment.

Timing:
- Start 66.1 s: the first moment "stopped past the line" coincides with red. If "vehicle stops" is read literally, the start would be about 65.0 s. Either choice changes IoU by less than 3%.
- End 102.1 s: green onset, per the class convention.

I agree with the first-pass annotator on all of the above.

Why confidence is medium, not high: the vehicles got past the line on green and yellow and were trapped by gridlock. A strict reading of "stops past the stop line ON red" (overshooting on arrival at a red) might exclude this. But what the camera sees, a car standing on the zebra through the whole red with pedestrians detouring around it, is exactly the stop_line state.

Side note, not part of this event: the white Chevrolet Cobalt that sat at the stop line behind the Mitsubishi pulls out at about 72.6-73.1 s on red. It passes the Mitsubishi on the right and goes through cw1 into the junction by about 75.6 s. This is a possible separate red_light candidate that should be checked on its own.

first.label: failure_to_yield
first.where: cw2 (outbound crossing), middle-right part x~1250-1560, y~480-545
first.description: Black BYD SUV (track 1983) comes in from the right edge and turns up-left through cw2 into the outbound without slowing. Two pedestrians (dark shirt with backpack, grey T-shirt) are walking right along the far half of cw2 inside its path. It passes about 0.3-1 m from them and hides their legs in frames 159.9-160.5. Main road red, so this is the cw2 pedestrian phase.

verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed. It fits the brief's definition: a vehicle drives through a crossing while pedestrians are on it.

Signal: the vehicle-head inset shows the top (red) lamp lit in every frame from 155.6 to 164.6 s. Many pedestrians are crossing cw1 and cw2 at the same time, so this is the pedestrian phase. Vehicles from the right side street are turning up-left through cw2 into the outbound at the same time.

Pedestrians: two men (dark shirt with backpack, and grey T-shirt) step off the median tip onto cw2 at about 157.2 s and walk right. At 159.0 s (zoomed frame, crop 1150-1750 x 400-620) both are clearly on the zebra stripes, the backpack man in the far third and the grey-shirt man in the middle. At 160.6 and 160.8 s (crop 1250-1700 x 430-610) their feet are still on the stripes, in the far half (about frame y 490-500 at x about 1468 and 1532).

Black BYD SUV: seen below cw2 at frame x about 1560-1800 at 158.6 s, moving left at a steady speed with no visible braking. In the 0.2 s and 0.25 s sheets it moves about the same distance every step from 158.6 to 161.0 s.
- Entry: at 159.4 s its front bumper is about 10 frame px below the zebra's near edge. At 159.5 s it is at the edge, and at 159.6-159.7 s it is on the stripes. Start = 159.5 s (+/-0.1).
- Passing the pedestrians: it drives up-left along the near half of cw2. From 159.8 to 160.4 s its roof hides the legs of both men, who are on the far half of the zebra just beyond it, roughly half a crossing width away (about 1-2 m; I cannot measure this more precisely).
- Exit: it then crosses the far half about 1-2 m behind (left of) the backpack man. At 161.0 s its rear bumper and rear wheel are on the far edge of the zebra. At 161.1 s the bumper is about 25 crop px past it (crop 1150-1450 x 420-570, 0.1 s steps). End = 161.1 s. The first-pass times (159.6 to 161.0 s) are close to these.

Skeptical caveat: this is the ordinary conflict between turning traffic and the cw2 pedestrian phase. The BYD crossed the far half of the zebra behind the men, and neither had to stop or change course. It still drove through the crosswalk without slowing while they were on it and passed very close. So under the brief's literal definition it counts.

Same class, adjacent in time (these affect the "simultaneous events = one segment" rule; I am leaving the merge decision to the orchestrator):
(a) A grey/white SUV right behind the BYD enters cw2 at about 161.1-161.3 s, just as the BYD leaves, and exits at about 162.25 s. From 161.5 to 161.8 s its roof hides the backpack man's legs, so it is as strong a case as the BYD.
(b) A white sedan is on cw2 from about 162.1 to 163.4 s. It crosses about 2-4 m behind the two men, which is a weaker case.
(c) Earlier, a dark SUV (on cw2 at 155.8 s, exiting about 156.6 s, with a man in a black cap walking left on cw2 next to it) and a green-and-black bus (on cw2 from about 156.9 to 158.6 s while the two men stepped on and walked toward it, 2-5 m away) also went through cw2 during the pedestrian phase.

If the orchestrator treats all of these as failure_to_yield, they merge into one continuous segment of roughly 155.x to 163.4 s. If only the two close passes are kept, the segment is 159.5 to about 162.25 s.

Minor notes:
- After about 162.5 s the two men drift slightly past the zebra's far edge (up to about 20 px at 163.9 s). This does not affect the BYD interval.
- The two women at the right end of cw2 (x about 1850) stand on the sidewalk the whole time and are not on the crossing.

first.label: failure_to_yield

verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:
I confirm this is failure_to_yield. Timing is 179.6 to 180.4 s. The first pass had 179.6 to 180.5, so the end is about 0.1 s earlier.

Signal: in the signal-head inset the bottom (green) lamp is lit from about 177.6 s and stays green through 184 s. Main-road green is the cw3 pedestrian phase, so the pedestrians on cw3 had right of way.

Vehicle: a white Chevrolet sedan of the Nexia/Aveo type, possibly with a small roof sign. It enters the frame at the right edge around x~1900, y~850 at about 178.0 s. It drives left along the bottom of the frame, across the lower part of cw3 (y about 950-1080), and on into the lower-left side street. Leftward flow there exists in the flow field, so the route is normal and this is not wrong_way.

Pedestrians: from 179.0 to 181.0 s one man in white is walking down the zebra (along its length) on the stripes. His feet move from about (721,941) to about (777,1030), on the right part of cw3 just below the island_3 tip. A second man in white follows him, and three women stand on the zebra further up-left. So a pedestrian is clearly on the crossing, in the same carriageway section the car passes through.

Pass: at 179.7-179.8 s his feet are at about y~970-975, and the near side of the car's footprint is about 25-30 px below that. Vehicles that used the slip lane passed at x about 206-221 (ids 77, 981, 3552). The x about 330-400 group is a through lane: 18 of 21 vehicles in it went straight to the bottom-right.

Path: the Spark drove straight past the slip-lane entry, across cw1 at about 276-277 s. It then crawled with the queue inside the junction until about 282.8 s (centre about (949,725), heading about 30 deg, the approach direction).

Turn start: in the 0.2 s zoom its body angle is the same at 282.8 and 283.0 s. The nose visibly swings toward the camera by 283.2-283.4 s. The track heading goes 31 -> 35 -> 41 -> 52 deg between about 283.0 and 283.9 s, so the turn starts at about 283.3 s.

Turn path: it passes the right (east) tip of island_3 at about 284.7 s (centre (1072,851), heading about 77-107 deg). It then heads left below island_3 (heading 139 deg at 285.1 s, 164 at 286.6, 175 at 287.2-287.7) and crosses the lower part of cw3 into the lower-left side street.

Turn end: the heading holds at about 176-177 deg from about 287.6-287.8 s, so the turn is complete at about 287.8 s. The car leaves the frame at the left edge at about 288.85 s. If the convention is 'leaves frame', use about 288.8.

That lane carries the cross street's straight-on traffic, not a designated right-turn path for the main road. The only other main-road vehicle that made this manoeuvre is id 95, at about 48-56 s. It came from the same lane and was also stuck in the junction queue. That looks like drivers leaving a spilled-back queue, which is still a turn from the wrong lane.

Doubt (why confidence is medium, not high): lane arrows are hidden under the queue, even in the background image. So I cannot rule out that this lane is marked straight+right. Even so, a right turn from it would normally go through the slip lane, not through the junction centre and the cross-street lane.

verdict.reasoning:
Where: cw3, the zebra across the lower-left side street. The pedestrian stands on the painted stripes, on the carriageway (not on the island), just past the right tip of island_tri2. I checked this in 1600 px zooms at 287.75, 289.25 and 300 s.

So she is a real crosser who got stuck mid-crossing, not someone passing by. The main-road head is green until about 288.0 s, yellow 288.5-291 s, then red, so she was on cw3 during her own green phase.

Vehicle 1, white Chevrolet Spark: it turns from the approach into the side-street carriageway below island_3. Its front reaches the right edge of the zebra at about 286.4 s (0.1 s zoom: bumper at the stripe ends at 286.3-286.5). Its rear clears the lower-left edge of the zebra at about 288.2 s; at 288.3 s it is past.

Vehicle 2, grey SUV: it comes off the right-turn slip lane. Its front bumper reaches the upper edge of the zebra at about 288.3-288.4 s. The Spark is the clearer case, since it crosses the part of the zebra ahead of her during her green. The SUV only passes behind her. The two crossings touch (Spark off at about 288.2, SUV on at about 288.3, a gap of 0.1 s or less) and involve the same pedestrian, so I keep them as one segment, 286.4-290.0. The Spark alone would be 286.4-288.2.

Doubts, and why confidence is medium rather than high: the pedestrian stands still the whole time and never steps into either vehicle's path, and she treats the island tip like a refuge. A stricter labeller could reject the SUV part (it crossed behind her), or the whole event (no conflict with her movement). There is no braking, swerving or contact, so near_miss does not fit either.

verdict.label: stop_line
verdict.reasoning:
I checked the frames myself and the event is real. The first-pass report is essentially right.

It arrives at 267-269 on green and stops behind a white Lacetti with a green plate. The Lacetti and a dark sedan are stuck in cw1 / the junction entrance (266-296). From about 269 the Cobalt stands wholly past the white stop line. The line runs under or behind its rear wheel, and its front wheels and bumper are at the upper edge of the cw1 zebra (clear at 303.5 zoom).

After the red onset at 291.3 it stays stationary past the line. At 294-296.5 the stuck cars in cw1 are still directly in front of it. Between 296.5 and 298.5 it reverses about 30 px, roughly 1 m (front bumper x moves back steadily in a 0.5 s crop sheet). It then stops again, still wholly past the line. From 299 to 327 it does not move (crop sheet every 3.5 s).

At 310.5-314 two pedestrians crossing cw1 on red have to walk around its front bumper. It never enters the junction and drives off only after green (about 328.3). The rest of the queue (a Nexia in the same lane, a Cobalt and others in the next lanes) stays behind the stop line.

Why it fits the class: it stands stopped past the stop line for the whole red phase, and after reversing it makes a fresh stop on red past the line (298.5). It never goes further into the intersection.

Why medium rather than high: the car went past the line legally on green and was trapped by the blocked junction. It did not overrun the line on red, so a stricter reading of the class might exclude it. The geometry and signal timing themselves are unambiguous.

Rejected: nothing else of this class in the window. The vehicles stuck in cw1 around 287-297 are a gridlock / blocked-junction situation, not stop_line.

first.label: failure_to_yield
first.where: Right half of cw2 (across the outbound carriageway), at about x 1420-1750.

verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:
What I saw, from a full sheet at 0.5 s over 300.1-309.8 s, crops at 0.5 s over 299-303.5 s, and crops at 0.2/0.25 s over 303.6-306.5 s:

- The vehicle signal is red throughout, so this is the pedestrian phase on cw2.
- Two girls (one in pink, one in white) step off the right sidewalk onto the far half of cw2 around 299 s, at full-frame x ~1720. They walk steadily left toward the median: x ~1590 at 301.5 s, ~1450 at 303.5 s, ~1400-1440 at 304.2 s, ~1350-1390 at 305.0 s, ~1325-1365 at 305.5 s. They reach the median/island area at ~1300 around 306.3 s. They never pause, look round or change pace.
- Dark-blue sedan (right-turner from the right-side road, heading up-left). Its front reaches the zebra at ~304.2 s at x ~1640, about 200 px (~4 m) right of the girls. It straddles the zebra at 304.4 s (x ~1590-1780, girls at ~1400-1430) and is off the far edge by ~304.8 s. The girls had crossed that stretch about 2 s earlier.
- White taxi with a roof sign. Its front reaches the zebra's near edge at ~304.9-305.0 s at x ~1545, about 150 px right of the girls. At 305.3 s its body is on the zebra at x ~1470-1640 and the girls' feet are at ~1350-1370. At 305.5 s its front is already past the far edge at x ~1420, about 60 px right of and beyond the girls. Its rear clears the zebra at ~305.7-305.9 s. It then carries on up-left into the outbound lanes above the zebra and never crosses the girls' remaining path. Its closest pass was about 1.5-2 m behind them.
- No other pedestrian was on cw2, or stepping onto it, anywhere in front of either car.

Verdict: the brief's literal wording is met, since pedestrians were on the crossing while vehicles drove through it. But both cars crossed only the part of the zebra the girls had already left and passed behind them. Neither pedestrian had to change speed or direction, and there was no evasive reaction. That means nobody was actually denied right of way. The recorded annotator convention in dev\decisions.md says the same thing: people the vehicle passes behind after they cleared its lane are not counted. The project README defines the class as a pedestrian "near the vehicle's path", which points the same way. So I reject this as failure_to_yield. No other class fits: this is an ordinary permitted right turn on the side road's green, with no near_miss braking or swerving.

Confidence is medium, not high, only because the literal one-line definition would count it and the taxi's pass was fairly close (~1.5-2 m behind). If the literal rule were applied, the merged segment for both cars would be 304.1-305.8 s: the sedan's front enters at ~304.1-304.2 s and the taxi's rear leaves at ~305.8 s. The first annotator's times already match that.

verdict.label: jaywalking
verdict.reasoning:
The frames support the first-pass report: a pedestrian was on the outbound carriageway, outside any crossing, with traffic passing him.

Start: 100.9 s, when he gets out of the car onto the road.
- 100.2 s: the right-side door of a white Lacetti opens. The car is stopped in the outbound curb lane beside the green bus at the stop (x~850, y~230).

- From 105 s he walks right along the curb lane, on the asphalt and clearly below the kerb and the planter wall. The sidewalk behind the planter is empty.
- Cars in the curb lane drive right past him: a white Land Cruiser at 105-106 s, a white SUV at 108 s, a black car at 110 s, and more at 116-124 s.
- He goes past the bus stop and along the planter (about 112-128 s) and stops at about 131.75 s at x~1600, y~455.

Waiting on the road, 131.75-146 s:
- A zoom at 138 s shows him standing on dark asphalt about 0.5 m from the planter's yellow kerb. That is roughly 25 px (about 1.5-2 m) above the top edge of the cw2 zebra, so he is not on the crossing.

- The main-road signal is red from about 140 s. At 146.0-146.1 s he starts walking, crossing with the pedestrian phase alongside the group that was waiting at the right end of cw2.

End: 146.2 s. The rule says the event ends when he leaves the road. He is on the carriageway outside the painted crossing the whole time up to this point. At 146.2 s he stops being a pedestrian loitering or walking in traffic and starts crossing with the signal at cw2. I did not use the first-pass end of 131.75 s, because he stays on the asphalt off the zebra for another 14 s after stopping.

Two caveats on the end time:
- A strict reading gives a later end. From 146 to about 155.5 s he walks about 1-1.5 m above the zebra's top edge and never steps onto the stripes (checked at 147-153 s). He only reaches the median tip at about 155.5 s. I treated crossing right next to the zebra, in the pedestrian phase with the crowd, as using the crossing, so I did not count it as jaywalking.
- Because he stays on the road until 146.2 s, this segment probably overlaps the next jaywalking event and should be merged with it, as the first-pass note predicted.

Why confidence is medium rather than high: his presence on the road is certain from 100.9 to at least 146 s, but walking along the road edge is not the typical way-across jaywalking case, and the end time depends on interpretation.

verdict.label: stop_line
verdict.reasoning:
The footage matches the first annotator's description, but the event does not meet the stop_line definition: "stops past the stop line on red without entering the intersection", ending when the signal turns green.

What I saw. I located the stop line on a clear frame at 87.0 s, cropped to x500-1300 and y380-720. It is the white line from about (500,530) to (890,485), just above cw1.
- Signal: flashing green around 74.3-74.8 s, yellow from about 75.3 s (still yellow at 78.0), red from about 78.25 s.
- Before red: the approach queue was already backed up from the junction. At 74.5 s the white Chevrolet Captiva's front was already over the stop line. From 74.5 to 78.25 s it crept forward about 30 px and stopped with its front at cw1's upper edge. The black Chery-type SUV in the lane nearest the median was already past the end of the stop line at 74.5 s (about x950, y505). Its front reached cw1 by 78.25 s.
- A white Kia Seltos ahead of them was on cw1 at red onset. It crawled into the junction during 79-81 s.
- So no vehicle crossed the stop line on red. The queue behind the Captiva, black cars at about x640 y437, stayed behind the line through 83.25 s.
- During red: both SUVs sat still past the stop line from 78.25 s. At step 0.2 the Captiva starts creeping at about 80.6 s and moves steadily from 81.0 s. The black SUV starts moving at about 81.4-81.6 s. Both then crossed cw1 (roughly 81.2 to 82.8 s) and drove into the junction while the signal was still red. By 83.3-84.3 s they were in the junction heading bottom-right.
- Pedestrians stepped onto cw1 from the left sidewalk at about 80.5 s. While the SUVs crossed, they were on the curb-side part of cw1, about 350-450 px (2-3 lanes) away, so there was no close conflict.

Why I reject it:
1. The vehicles did not stop on red. They got stuck in a spill-back queue on flashing green and yellow.
2. They did enter the intersection, on red.
3. The end point the convention requires (signal turns green) never happens. They left about 3 s into the red phase.

Other classes fit no better:
- red_light: their fronts crossed the stop line on green or yellow, so its start point was not on red.
- failure_to_yield: it technically applies, since pedestrians were on cw1 while the SUVs crossed. But the pedestrians were several lanes away, so I would not relabel to it.

A dwell time on red of about 2.4-3.3 s is also a thin basis for a violation. The first annotator had the same doubts and gave low confidence, so I recommend dropping this event.

If the team decides to count spill-back vehicles stuck past the stop line at red onset, use stop_line, start 78.25 s (red onset, both already stationary past the line), end about 81.5 s (the SUV departs; the Captiva is already creeping from 80.6 s). Note in that case that they then went through on red.

verdict.label: stop_line
verdict.reasoning:
Verdict: reject. The facts are as the first pass reported, but the event does not fit the stop_line definition. The two SUVs were stuck behind a car waiting to U-turn, which is box-blocking, and then they cleared the junction on red. That is the same pattern the team already rejected in C3902 at 78.25.

What I saw:
- **Signal (crop 1130-360-1180-415, 0.05 s steps).** Green flashes at 55.0-55.5. Yellow (middle lamp) is lit from 55.75 to 58.6. The top red lamp is first lit at 58.70, so red onset is about 58.65-58.70. Red then lasts past 80 s.
- **History (sheets 36-53, crop 700-350-1400-700).** A grey Cobalt stops at the median tip on cw1 from about 37 s, waiting to U-turn. The red crossover SUV pulls up behind it at about 39-40 s on green, and the white Chevrolet Tracker stops behind the red SUV by about 42-43 s. Both crossed the stop line on green. By red onset they had been standing still for about 15 s.
- **56.7-63.5 (0.25 s zooms).** The red SUV stands wholly past the stop line, with its nose at cw1's upper edge. The Tracker's rear wheels are at the white stop line and its front wheels are about 30-40 px (roughly 1-1.5 m) past it, at about (917, 501). Neither vehicle moves. The Cobalt starts inching forward at about 63.3-63.5.
- **Red SUV.** It starts creeping at 64.25-64.5 and is clearly moving by 64.75. It crosses cw1 and is out of the stop zone at about 66.5, then drives straight through the junction toward the bottom-right, on red.
- **Tracker.** Its plate stays fixed through 64.75. It moves slightly at 65.0 and clearly by 65.25-65.5. It crawls forward to the median nose (65.25-67.5), crosses cw1 at 67.5-68.5 and drives through the junction by 69.5, still on red.
- **Afterwards.** Pedestrians start onto cw1 at about 69.

Checked against the brief's definition ("stops past the stop line on red without entering the intersection", start = vehicle stops, end = signal turns green), all three parts fail:
1. They stopped on green (about 40-43 s), not on red.
2. Both entered the intersection on red (red SUV from 64.3, Tracker from 65.0).
3. They left about 6 s into red, not when the signal turned green.

The accepted stop_line precedents are different: C3896 291.3-327.4 (a Cobalt at the median nose) and 66.1-102.1 (a black sedan). In both, the car stood past the line for the whole red and never went into the junction. This case matches the C3902 78.25 case that was rejected as gridlock: caught past the line at red onset, then drove into the junction on red. The only difference is that these SUVs stood about 6 s into red instead of about 3 s.

red_light does not fit either, because they crossed the stop line on green. No class covers blocking the box and then clearing the junction on red. Labelling this stop_line would teach the detector to fire on vehicles caught in a queue.

If the team adopts the looser rule ("any vehicle stationary past the stop line during red"), the window is 58.7 (red onset) to 65.0, when the last vehicle (the Tracker) starts moving. The start and end fields hold those values. Alternative ends: 64.3 if only the red SUV counts, or about 68.3 if the event runs until the Tracker leaves the stop zone.

Doubtful things I noticed but did not verify:
- **White sedan crossing cw1 at 58.7.** It was already on cw1 at red onset, so it probably crossed the line on yellow. Not red_light, but it is worth checking.
- **Grey Cobalt stopped at about (1530, 530) on cw2 from about 67 to beyond 80 s.** It was waiting to U-turn, so this is not a stop_line event, but it could be checked separately.

Why the U-turn is not illegal:

The median tip carries only a pedestrian-crossing sign. Island_round carries only the blue keep-right sign (4.2.1). This sign faces the junction, and a U-turner heading up-left keeps the island on its left, so the sign channels this manoeuvre rather than banning it. The sign on the gantry is diamond-shaped (its back is visible), so it is a main-road sign.

- The car turned from the leftmost (median) lane after waiting in the junction, which is normal behaviour for a car turning left or U-turning.

- The main-road signal is red for the whole of 59.5-70 s, so pedestrians have their phase.

Start and end:

- End 65.9: the rear leaves cw2.

Why medium confidence:
- The label changes class from what was reported.
- The car passed a few metres ahead of the group rather than forcing anyone to stop, although by the brief's rule ("while a pedestrian is on it") it qualifies.

Other notes:

A vehicle that stood past the stop line when the signal turned red and then drove on into the junction during red is "neither stop_line nor red_light: they crossed the line on green". stop_line does not fit either, because it did enter the junction before green. Under a looser, traffic-law reading ("entered the junction on red after stopping past the line") it would count as a red-light violation. That is why confidence is only medium rather than high.

Rejected alternative, failure_to_yield on cw1 from about 137.8 to 139.3 s. Pedestrians stepped onto cw1 from the left kerb at about 136.3 s. The pedestrian signal head I checked on the gantry pole shows red throughout; per the brief it follows the main-road phase, so it does not tell us about cw1. While the SUV crossed the right half of cw1, the leading pedestrian was on the left half:
- at 137.8 s: about x542 against the SUV's left side at about x700 (about 3 m, roughly 0.2-0.28 of the crossing length);
- at 139.2 s: about x649 against the SUV at x890-1110 (about 5 m, roughly 0.4).
The pedestrian was walking toward the SUV's lane but never broke stride. The SUV pulled away before the pedestrians reached its path. This is borderline under the dev convention (a pedestrian close to the vehicle's crossing point, not "far along the crossing"), so I do not endorse it; at most it is a low-confidence candidate.

first.label: failure_to_yield

verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:

- Its front reaches the top edge of the zebra at about 109.2 and is on the stripes by 109.4, so it enters at about 109.25.
- Its rear clears the left edge of cw3 at about 110.5: at 110.4 the rear is still at the edge, and at 110.6 it is off.
- So the vehicle is on the crossing for 109.25-110.5, not 109.75-111.25 as the first pass reported.

The pedestrians and the layout: the two young men (white shirt, and backpack) are walking slowly up-left along cw3 toward the gantry corner. The islands split the side street into two carriageways:
- The upper one is outbound, between the gantry-corner curb and the line joining the tips of island_tri2 and island_3. The Cobalt was in its curb lane.
- The lower one is inbound.

Where the men were while the car was on the crossing:
- For the whole of 109.25-110.5, both men's feet were on the lower side of the island-tip line, at the median gap. At 109.0 their feet were near frame (620-650, 965-980); at 110.55 near (550-615, 875-925).

The men were about 4-5 m away, still on the other carriageway, and unaffected. That is not clear evidence of failure_to_yield, so I default to false.

If the ground truth instead counts any pedestrian anywhere on the cw3 polygon, use 109.25-110.5 (label failure_to_yield). In that case this should be merged with the preceding first-Cobalt segment, as the first pass suggested. The men were even farther away during that earlier pass.

The start is about 3 s early, and the true end is much later than 176.5. My start is high confidence; the end is only medium confidence.

Items 2 and 3 of the first pass are confirmed:

- From about 156, a group of students walks from cw2 up to the planter wall, then up-left in the gutter: 162 at x~1420-1480, 170 at x~1270-1310. They are still on the asphalt at 171.

WHY 176.5 IS NOT THE END
- A young woman in a black top and jeans, holding papers, walks in the gutter along the wall from about 151.
- From about 156-158 until about 218 she stands still on the asphalt at the foot of the planter wall, at about (1544, 425).
- At high zoom (165 s) her feet are clearly on the road surface, with the wall face behind her and a car passing about 1 m away.

- At 218-222 she walks out onto the road to meet two friends who came diagonally off cw2. The three reach cw2 at about 222.75-223.

Overlap with the next pedestrian wave (same class, so one segment under the brief):

I stopped at 237.5 because a separate segment starting about 239.5 is equally defensible. Please merge this with any first-pass jaywalking segments from about 219 onward.
2. Two people who stand at the median tip / cw2 from 238 to 276 are rejected: standing on the median is not jaywalking.
3. The people walking on the cw2 zebra at 146-153 and 222-226 are legal crossers, not jaywalkers.

first.label: jaywalking

verdict.label: jaywalking
verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed as jaywalking. The main-road signal inset shows red for the whole 8-25 s window. I followed the man in the dark olive polo with the white-trimmed collar, carrying a black bag.

Path, from full-frame sheets at 0.5 s steps and crop zooms at 0.2 s:
- 9.5-11.0 s: he comes off the median/island_round end and walks right-to-left along cw1, near its lower edge. At 11.0 s both feet are still on the lower ends of the stripes (~x950,y590).
- 11.4 s: in the 10x zoom his leading foot is about 5 px (~0.5 m) past the painted stripe ends.
- 11.6 s: the front foot is clearly past the ends and the rear foot is at the edge.
- 11.8-12.0 s: both feet are 7-10 px off the zebra. From 12.2 s his path turns steeply down-left, away from cw1's slope (~0.5 against ~0.12), across the open junction asphalt: (891,570) at 12.5 s, (816,600) at 14 s, (744,660) at 16 s.

Walking 8-10 m diagonally across the junction box, off any zebra, is plainly a pedestrian on the carriageway outside a crossing. The flow field shows vehicle traffic through this area.

Boundaries:
- Start 11.6 s (+/-0.2): the first frame where a foot is clearly past cw1's lower edge. The first-pass value of 12.0 s is a bit late, since both feet are already off at 11.8 s.
- End 20.5 s (+/-0.2): when he steps up onto island_3. The first-pass value of 21.0 s is a bit late, since at 20.6-21.0 s he is already on the paving.
- Strictly, the ~1 s on island_tri1's tip (17.0-18.0 s) would split this into 11.6-17.0 and 18.0-20.5. I kept one segment because it is one continuous crossing and he never stops on that island.

Proposed extension, rejected. From about 15.5 s to 23.5 s the teal-top woman walks along cw2's far (upper) edge. From about 19 s she follows the base of the grass-strip kerb, 12-25 px (roughly 1.5-2.5 m) past the stripe ends. At about 23.5-23.8 s she steps up at the kerb corner (~x1745,y410). She is following the crossing's line and cutting its end rather than walking out into traffic, so it is ambiguous. I agree with the first pass that it should not be counted, so the end stays at 20.5 s and does not move to 23.5.

Separate later case, outside this segment: at about 27-28 s the same man steps down from island_3's lower kerb and walks down along cw3's right edge, partly just outside the stripes, until about 33 s. It is borderline, and it is separated from this event by about 7 s standing on the island.

first.label: failure_to_yield
first.where: cw2 (across the outbound carriageway, right sidewalk to median tip), x~1200-1880, y~470-540
first.description: A man in a light-blue shirt crosses cw2 from right to left, starting at 19.75 s and reaching the median tip at about 28.0 s, while the main road is red. verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed on cw2 (full-frame x~1180-1880, y~470-545). The main-road head is red from 15.5 to 31 s, and a crowd is crossing cw1 at the same time, so this is the normal pedestrian phase. A man in a light-blue shirt and dark trousers reaches the right-hand curb at about 19.4 s. He steps onto the zebra at about 19.7 s: at 19.9 s his feet are on the stripes at about (1766,485). He walks right to left along the upper, far part of the stripes (about 1592,496 at 22.0 s; 1313,517 at 26.0 s; 1223,528 at 27.9 s). He reaches the median tip at about 28.4-28.6 s and then walks along the median. Right-side traffic keeps driving through cw2 into the outbound the whole time and never stops for him.
(1) White Nexia sedan. It crawls up to the near edge of the zebra from 19.6 s. Its front bumper reaches the near stripe edge at about 20.3 s (full ~1556,526, checked at 0.1 s steps). It crosses at x~1450-1600, 1-3 m ahead of him (he is at x~1730), and is clear by about 21.2 s.
(2) Black SUV. It enters at about 21.0 s, crosses at x~1450-1700 just ahead of and beside him, and is clear by about 21.75 s.
(3) White flower-delivery box truck. It creeps at the near edge from 21.4 to 22.5 s, is on the crossing about 22.5-25.3 s behind him (at x 1600-1700), then overtakes him on the far side at about 24.5 s.
(4) Green bus 01045. It crosses the right part of cw2 at about 24.5-27 s, well behind him.
(5) White Sonata-type sedan. It is on the crossing about 25.3-27.3 s behind him, then passes him on the far side.
(6) White BMW X5. It enters at about 27.4 s and crosses at x~1320-1420, just behind him. At 27.9-28.0 s it passes about 0.5-1 m from him on the far side, as he nears the median tip. Its rear wheel crosses the far stripe edge at about 28.0 s (checked at 0.1 s steps).
He is on the crossing without a break from 19.7 to about 28.4 s. At every moment from 20.3 to 28.0 s at least one vehicle is on the crossing or straddling its near edge (the only possible gap is about 21.8-22.5 s while the box truck creeps at the edge), so this is ONE merged segment.
Start: I use 20.3 s (the Nexia entering), not 19.5 s. At 19.5 s the Nexia is still below the zebra. The black crossover ahead of it had entered the crossing before 18.5 s, while the man was still walking along the sidewalk, and he let it pass, so it is not a failure to yield. If you count him stepping on while that crossover's rear was still on the stripes, the earliest defensible start is about 19.7 s.
End: 28.0 s, when the X5 clears.
Excluded: green bus 01328 (it enters the right end of cw2 at about 28.8-29.2 s, when he is already at the median tip about 600 px away), and a woman in white trousers who stays on the far sidewalk.
Caveat: only the Nexia and the black SUV cross clearly ahead of him in his path. The X5 passes close behind him (about 1 m), and the box truck, bus 01045 and the Sonata cross the part of the crossing he has already walked. They still meet the brief's literal definition ("drives through a crossing while a pedestrian is on it"), and that is what I used. Under a stricter "must cross ahead of the pedestrian" reading, the core segment would be only about 20.3-21.8 s. No hard braking or swerving is seen, so this is not a near_miss.

first.label: stopped_vehicle
first.where: Outbound bus lane at the 'OQ' bus stop, about x 589-780, y 130-200
first.description: BUS AT THE BUS STOP (policy decision): dark-grey/green electric bus, route 57 (fleet no. about 01045). Arrives from the right, stops about 36.75 s, departs up-left about 52.75 s. Normal dwell.

verdict.label: stopped_vehicle
verdict.reasoning:
What happens in the video matches the first-pass description, and the times are right. I am rejecting it because it is a scheduled bus stopping at a marked bus stop, not a stopped-vehicle incident.

Timeline, from crop zooms of x 450-1100, y 40-280 at 0.2 s steps:
- A dark-grey/green electric bus (route 57 on the destination display, fleet number 01 045) moves up-left in the curb lane of the outbound carriageway. Its front edge moves steadily left between 34.4 s and 36.4 s, slows down, and stops at about 36.6-36.8 s, beside the 'Avtokredit' shelter and just before the 'OQ' shelter.
- The bus stays still and passengers get on and off. At 52.0, 52.2 and 52.4 s its front edge and rear wheel are at the same place.
- It starts creeping forward at about 52.6-52.8 s, is clearly moving by 53.0-53.6 s, and has left the stop area by about 56 s.
- If it were counted, the stop would run from about 36.7 s to 52.7 s (16 s). The first-pass 36.75 s / 52.75 s is accurate.

Why I am not counting it:
1. This is normal operation of a public-transport stop, not an anomaly. The vehicle does not break down, park illegally or block traffic without reason. Other cars pass it on the left the whole time.
2. The brief treats the bus stop as a normal feature of the scene ("Passengers boarding a bus at the bus stop are not on the carriageway"). It also excludes normal, expected stops (a queue at a signal) from stopped_vehicle. A timetabled stop at a marked bus stop falls under the same idea.
3. The stop is in use all the time. A green route-68 bus (fleet number about 01 528) pulls up behind at about 41.8 s and stays until about 66-68 s. A green articulated route-14 bus then stops at the 'OQ' shelter from about 72 s and is still there at 88 s. Counting bus stops would mean one long stopped_vehicle segment covering most of the video. That would teach the detector to fire on every bus stop.

My confidence is only medium because this is a question of policy, not of what the video shows. Read literally, the class definition ("stationary on the carriageway >= 10 s, not in a signal queue") could cover a curb-lane bus stop. If the team decides that bus stops count, use start 36.7 s and end 52.7 s for the route-57 bus. The rule that simultaneous events of the same class form one segment would then stretch that segment to cover the route-68 and route-14 buses as well, to about 88 s or later. Default: not an event.

Timing, from the 0.1 s crops:

2. The main road was red. cw3 is normally crossed while the main road is green, so cw3's pedestrian phase was probably red and the car from the right side road probably had green, which makes a right-of-way violation arguable.

verdict.label: illegal_u_turn
verdict.reasoning:
I rejected this as illegal_u_turn. The manoeuvre happened, but nothing I could see prohibits it, and the class needs "U-turn where markings/signs prohibit it".

What I saw:
- 73-75 s (yellow; the signal goes red at ~76): the white Labo-type pickup with a grey canopy is already next to the median, past the stop line's median end (x~1000-1135, y~446-500 at 75.0). It crossed the stop line on yellow, so it is not red_light by the brief's convention. From 75.5 to 79.5 it creeps along the median, mostly hidden behind the semi-trailer.
- 84.75-86.5: it drives east past the median tip and island_round (x~1310 -> 1460, y~510-525). It keeps island_round on its left, which obeys the keep-right sign on that island.
- 96.5-98.4: it stands facing up, with its rear wheels at cw2's lower edge (x~1500-1580). Two pedestrians (one in a white cap) cross cw2 just in front of it and pass on its right (97.6-98.4). Its brake lights are on until ~98.4.
- 98.6-100.8: it moves off only after they have cleared its front and swings left. By ~100.25-100.75 it is lined up with the outbound lanes heading up-left, which completes the U-turn around the median tip. A white car and a black car from the right follow it through cw2.

Why I rejected it:
1. Signage at the tip, checked in a zoomed frame at 60 s: the median-tip signal head, a blue pedestrian-crossing sign, and a keep-right sign on island_round, which the pickup obeyed. There is no no-U-turn or no-left-turn sign. The approach gantry holds signal heads and one diamond-shaped sign seen from behind; it is not a U-turn prohibition.
2. Markings: no solid line or other marking closes the gap between the median tip and island_round. The median lane was always occupied, so I could not see whether it has a lane arrow; that is one reason confidence is not high.
3. Normal flow: flow_field.jpg has yellow arrows along exactly this path (east past the median tip, then up into the outbound), so this is a recurring manoeuvre here, not an anomaly.
4. Conduct: the pickup made the U-turn from the leftmost (median) lane. It had entered on yellow and was clearing the junction, and it waited for pedestrians before moving off.

Other classes do not fit this window either:
- red_light: it crossed the stop line before red onset.
- failure_to_yield: it waited for the crossing pedestrians, and the people near island_round stayed more than 150 px from its path.

The only possible side note is a separate, weak stop_line case: it stood past the stop line from ~76 to 80.75 on red. It later entered the junction, though, so it does not really meet that definition either.

The start and end values (98.4 to 100.8) are my refined timing of the left swing out of cw2, given for reference only. If the approach-side pre-positioning is counted, the whole U-turn runs from ~84 to 100.8.

- About 82-86 s: it comes from the approach side along the junction and drives right (east), just below cw2.
- 87.4-88.4 s: it turns north onto cw2. Its brake lights come on and it stops at about 88.4 with the front part of the vehicle over the zebra (about x 1500-1580, y 450-560). Three young men (two in black, one in a white shirt with a backpack) are crossing cw2 from right to left. They walk past just beyond its nose at 88.4-89.2 without stopping or changing course. The white-shirt man was already running at 87.4, before the pickup turned, so that is not an evasive reaction.
- 89-98 s: it stays stopped for about 10 s while a steady stream of pedestrians crosses cw2 in front of its nose. The main-road signal is red, so pedestrians have their phase.
- 97.6-98.6 s: the last close pair, two young men walking left to right with one in a white cap, pass directly beyond its nose. By 98.4-98.6 they are past its front-right corner. At 98.4-98.6 the pickup's left rear lamp shows amber (probably the left indicator), and it starts turning left at about 98.5-98.8. At that moment the pair are about 0.5-1 m to its right and still on the zebra, but outside its path. It turns away from them, and their pace stays steady in every frame from 98.6 to 99.6. Nobody brakes, steps back or swerves.
- 99.4-101.2 s: the pedestrians on the left end of cw2 are standing at the median tip or round island near the sign (x about 1100-1220). They are several metres from the pickup's path, which goes up-left into the outbound carriageway.
- About 100.2-100.4 s: its rear wheels clear the top edge of cw2.

Pedestrians were on cw2 while it moved off, so the literal wording is technically met. But nobody's path was cut and nobody took evasive action, and the vehicle had stopped and waited about 10 s. So I label this not real.

If a reviewer counts it anyway, use about 98.5 (starts moving) to 100.3 (rear clears cw2). Under the 'vehicle enters crossing' rule the start could instead be about 87.8, when it first rolled onto the zebra.

Doubtful and rejected: the pickup stopped with its front on cw2 from about 88.4 to 98.5. That is encroachment or blocking, not failure_to_yield, and the pedestrians walked past its nose without deviating.

Separate lead, not verified closely: this pickup's whole route, from the approach side on red at about 82-86 through a turn into the outbound carriageway, looks like a U-turn. Whether it is an illegal_u_turn or red_light event should be judged separately.

verdict.label: jaywalking
verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed as jaywalking. From 100.6 s to about 116 s at least one pedestrian is always on the junction asphalt between cw1 and cw3, well away from both zebras and the kerb.

At 100.6 both feet are just below the stripes on the asphalt, and at 100.8 he is clearly off. So I set the start at 100.6, a little earlier than the first annotator's 100.75. Nobody was on this asphalt between 96.8 and 100.4.

- from about 106.3, a man in black with beige trousers, and a second man in black with a bag;
- from about 110.5, a young man in a dark polo and a man in a light-blue shirt.
At 112.0, for example, the polo man is at about (531,690) and the light-blue man at about (437,697). Both are on bare asphalt between cw1 and island_tri1.

End: the last people on the asphalt are the polo man and the light-blue man.
- Against the painted stripes (0.2 s zoom, crop 360-730-560-830): the polo man reaches them at about 115.6-115.8 and the light-blue man at about 116.0. At 115.0 the light-blue man's feet are still about 17 px above the stripe ends, and at 116.2-116.4 he is on them.
- Against the layout's cw3 polygon, whose edge sits about 25 px higher than the paint at x≈420, he crosses at about 114.8-115.0. That matches the first annotator's 115.0.
I report 116.0, based on the visible paint; if polygon membership is the rule, use about 115.0.

No other person enters this asphalt after them in 116-119.75. A man in white trousers after 117.75 is on cw1 itself, and the bearded man in a black cap walked on the sidewalk and then onto cw3, so neither counts.

The main-road signal is red until about 114.5 (red+yellow from about 111.8, green by 114.8), so no turning vehicle came near these people. That does not affect the class, which only asks whether a pedestrian is on the carriageway outside a crossing. The one doubt is interpretive: this is corner-cutting between two adjacent zebras. On the evidence, though, people were clearly on the carriageway, several metres long and continuously for about 15 s.

first.label: failure_to_yield
first.where: cw3 middle-lower section (x~400-950, y~830-1060), plus cw2 right half (x~1500-1700, y~440-520)
first.description: Main road red. Three vehicles in one merged segment. (a) A black Chevrolet sedan from the right side street crossed cw3 westward (107.6-109.4). It passed ~0.5-1 m in front of a man in a blue shirt walking down the zebra (108.25-109.0). (b) A white Daewoo Nexia followed (110.0-111.6). It passed ~0.3-0.5 m in front of the same man, who stopped, and a young man in a white shirt with a backpack. (c) At the same time a white Chevrolet Cobalt from the right street drove up-left through cw2 (108.75-110.6). It passed ~0.3-0.5 m from a man in a white shirt walking right along cw2's upper edge. Caveats: the cw3 pedestrians were crossing against the cw3 pedestrian red (gantry pedestrian head red, like C3897 213.8-216.9, labelled low), and the cw2 man was on or just above the zebra's top edge.

verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:
Signals: the main-road head is red through 111.1. It shows red+yellow from about 111.6 and green by 114.6. The gantry pedestrian head (x≈267, y≈500) is red the whole time from 107 to 112.

(c) cw2, the strongest part. A white Chevrolet Cobalt from the right street is turning up-left into the outbound carriageway. Its nose had been sitting on the lower part of cw2 in a jam since about 104.5 (front at x≈1650→1620). A man in a white shirt steps off the median tip onto cw2 at about 103.0 and walks right along the zebra's upper edge, feet at y≈480-490. Because the main road is red, cw2 pedestrians have their phase, so the turning car should yield. Positions (x):
- 108.0: man at 1560, Cobalt front at 1606, the car crawling (about 25 px/s).
- 108.6-108.8: the man passes directly in front of or at the Cobalt's nose (man ~1596, front ~1582). The car keeps rolling instead of stopping.
- 109.2-110.0: the car speeds up (front 1563→1488) and drives past his side. Its roof hides his legs at 109.2-109.8, so it passed about 0.3-0.6 m from him.
- ~110.8: the Cobalt's rear leaves the upper edge of cw2.
He kept walking the whole time.

(a) cw3. A black Chevrolet from the right drives straight into the lower-left side street. Its front reaches the right edge of cw3 at about 107.6 (checked at 0.2 s steps) and its rear clears the left edge at about 109.5. At 108.4 it passes about 1-2 m in front of a man in a blue shirt walking down the zebra (feet ~y 870, car's upper edge ~y 880-900).

(b) cw3. A white Daewoo Nexia enters cw3 at about 109.9 and leaves at about 111.6. The rear clears the left edge between 111.4 and 111.6. The man in blue stands still from about 110.3 to 111.3 to let it pass, just above its roofline (about 0.3-0.5 m). A young man in a white shirt with a backpack is also on the zebra.

Verdict: all three match the brief's literal definition: a vehicle drives through a crossing while a pedestrian is on it. For (a) and (b) there is a big caveat. The cw3 pedestrians are crossing against the red pedestrian head (they are a stream coming off cw1), and the cars going straight have their own green, so the driver arguably had right of way. On their own I would rate (a) and (b) low. (c) is a real case: a turning vehicle on the pedestrians' phase rolls past a crossing pedestrian's nose and then passes within about 0.5 m of him. The only doubt is that he walked right on the zebra's upper edge, because jammed cars were blocking the zebra.

Same-class events at the same time are merged into one segment. So the segment runs from the black car entering cw3 (107.6) to the Nexia leaving cw3 (111.6), and the Cobalt's cw2 pass (about 108.0-110.8) falls inside it. If reviewers exclude the cw3 pedestrians because they crossed on red, the segment would shrink to about 108.0-110.8 (cw2 Cobalt only). I agree with the first-pass bounds.

first.label: failure_to_yield
first.where: cw2, right (kerb) end by the driveway mouth, x~1540-1830, y~490-590
first.description: Main road red, so this is the pedestrian phase. A black Chevrolet Epica-type sedan turns from the right-side road up-left into the outbound carriageway and cuts through the right end of cw2. A man in a white shirt (phone at ear, briefcase) had stepped out of the waiting group onto the zebra's end at 242.25 and kept walking. The car passed about 1 m in front of him (242.5-243.0) and he walked on right behind it. The car's front reaches the zebra at ~242.6 and its rear clears the upper edge at ~244.4. Only medium confidence: he was at the very kerb end of the crossing, and the 4.67 s precedent rejected pedestrians who stayed at the waiting spot. He did not stay: he was already moving onto the crossing.

verdict.label: failure_to_yield
verdict.reasoning:
I confirm the event, with small changes to the times: 242.9-244.3 s instead of 242.6-244.4 s.

Signal: the vehicle head showed flashing green at about 230-233 s, yellow at 236.75 s and red from about 237.5 s through 248 s. Pedestrians were crossing cw1 at 238.6 s and 242.6 s, so this is the main-road-red pedestrian phase.

Setting: a waiting group stood at the kerb end of cw2 (x about 1690-1830, y about 450-520) from at least 233 s. Some of them stood on the ends of the zebra stripes. Cars kept turning up-left through the right end of cw2 into the outbound carriageway: a white car at 239 s, a white SUV at 240 s, a black SUV at 241.4 s, then the black Chevrolet Epica-type sedan. The black SUV passed right beside the standing group, but those people stayed put, so under the 4.67 s precedent that is not an event.

The pedestrian: I tracked his feet with 0.2 s crops. The man in the white shirt (phone at ear, briefcase) stood still at about (1805,510) at 241.4-241.6 s. From 241.8 s he walked steadily down-left onto the crossing: (1796,513) at 242.0 s, (1788,519) at 242.4 s, (1784,520) at 242.6 s, (1771,520) at 243.0 s, (1754,523) at 243.4 s, (1728,522) at 244.0 s, (1693,524) at 244.6 s. The stripes end at about x 1785-1800, so from about 242.4 s he was on the crossing's right end, along its near (lower) edge. His legs show a walking stride in the 242.2-242.4 s frames. He walked slowly while the car passed (about 0.7 m/s) and faster once it had gone (about 1.3 m/s), passing right behind it.

The car: at 242.0-242.4 s it was pointed straight up the image, toward the spot where he stood. It then curved left across his walking path, about 2-3 m ahead of him along the crossing, and never slowed. After it passed, the whole group started across at about 244.6-245.4 s, and no more cars came.

Timing, judged from the wheels' ground contact rather than where the car body overlaps the stripes. The zebra's near edge is at about y 523-531 for x 1600-1665, and its far edge at about y 497-505 for x 1450-1570. At 242.6 s the front-left wheel was at about (1677,575), roughly 2 m short of the zebra, so 242.6 s is too early; the body only looks like it is on the zebra because of its height. The front-right corner reaches the near edge at about 243.0 s and the front-left corner at about 243.2 s, so start is about 242.9-243.0 s. The rear bumper's ground line reaches the far edge at about 244.2 s and has cleared it by 244.4 s (ground about y 492 against the edge at about 504), so end is about 244.3 s.

Why only medium confidence: he was at the very kerb end of a long crossing and never had to stop or step back. The car's path through the zebra was about 2-4 m from him along the crossing. I could not read the cw2 pedestrian signal directly; I am relying on the scene fact that cw2 has the pedestrian phase while the main road is red. What makes this different from the rejected waiting-group cases is that he had clearly left the waiting spot and was walking on the crossing about 1 s before the car reached it.

first.label: jaywalking
first.where: outbound carriageway from the upper edge of cw2 (x~1340, y~515) diagonally to the grass-strip wall base, then along the gutter to the far sidewalk (x~1215, y~312); also the junction corner between cw1, island_tri1 and cw3
first.description: Main road red. Man in black (black shirt and trousers, shoulder bag; track 3582) walks along cw2's upper edge from the median tip. At ~251.75 he veers off it, crosses the outbound lanes diagonally (a black sedan passes near him at 250-251), reaches the wall base at ~258 and walks in the gutter up-left.
